text: governs.live_truth names a file, and the truth a rule is about is routinely a symbol inside one — an allowlist constant, a registry dict, a base class. Measured over aix-platform's 37 declaring rules on 2026-09-05: after the list grammar landed, 8 still fail, every one because live_truth spells 'path.py:NAME' and literal_relative refuses the colon. Splitting the anchor is cheap; deciding whether the symbol still EXISTS is not, and it is the same question harnex's evidence verifier answers by counting literal occurrences with a character-class boundary — the mechanism that produced the only regression this project has shipped. So the gap is real and its cheap fix is the wrong one: a path check that accepted 'registry.py:RULES' and only stat'd 'registry.py' would report a live truth for a symbol that was deleted, which is the silent staleness the auditor exists to catch. Either the anchor stays a file and the shape error stands, or live_truth learns the language.
source: aix-platform probe after cafda13, 2026-09-05; the 8 residual findings read
